newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Montell margins up vs Q1 96, down vs Q4 96.
newsitem.headline: Montell margins up vs Q1 96, down vs Q4 96.

text.p: Plastics producer Montell Polyelofins said margins for its products in the first quarter of 1997 were higher than in the same period of 1996 but lower than in the final quarter of last year.

Montell -- a polypropylene and polyethylene joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell and Italy's Montedison -- reported an operating profit of $69 million for the first quarter, versus $42 million for the same period of 1996.
It attributed the earnings increase to cost-efficiency programmes and higher polypropylene margins in Europe compared with the first quarter of 1996.

However, the company said that while selling prices for polyolefins had been rising during the first quarter of 1997, this had not been enough to offset the rise in the prices it had to pay for olefin feedstocks.

The company quoted chief executive Peter Vogtlaender as saying: "I am encouraged by the growth in polypropylene demand that has continued during the first quarter. This has allowed the new capacity to be absorbed without significant disruption to the industry."
"Unfortunately, while prices have been increasing they have not been sufficient to offset the rising olefins feedstock costs, resulting in reduced margins."
In the fourth quarter of 1996 Montell had posted an operating profit of $92 million.
